name: South Face

pitch_detail.notes: Start near the 'Confession Box' feature described in the FA account.
A spectacular curving chimney climbed on aid by the FA party, then fine free cracks higher; 'Pulpit Ledge' is in this section.
Passes 'Belfry Ledge' near the top before easier ground to the summit.

descent_text: Descend west off the summit via the regular class-3 walk-up route, the same descent used by the NE Ridge route; involves loose talus and some downclimbing back toward camp.
approach: The drive itself is easy — paved the whole way from Winthrop up the Chewuch River valley to the Andrews Creek Trailhead, about 24 miles total — but the climb to Cathedral Peak is one of the longest wilderness approaches in the state. From the trailhead, the Andrews Creek Trail (#504) climbs roughly 12 miles to 6,680+ ft Andrews Pass, then descends into the Spanish Creek drainage before a side trail climbs to Upper Cathedral Lakes below the peak's southwest side, putting the one-way approach at around 18 miles with significant elevation gain and loss along the way. Most parties treat this as a 2-4 day backpack (roughly 40+ miles round trip), camping at or near Cathedral Lakes before making a summit push. A free self-issue wilderness permit is required at the trailhead, along with a trailhead parking pass; the first many miles are a hot, rocky, buggy uphill slog with little shade, so this is genuinely a remote, multi-day alpine objective rather than a day-approach crag. For this specific route: from Cathedral Lakes camp, follow the trail toward Cathedral Pass and climb scree/talus to the base of the peak's main South Face and start low in the centre of the open wall, left of the deep gully that separates Cathedral Peak from The Monk (the SE Buttress starts inside that gully).
overview: The original 1968 Beckey line up the middle of Cathedral's imposing ~1,000-foot South Face — a classic granite climb at 5.8 with some original A1 aid, which can be led free.
beta: Follows a classic line up the middle of the South Face. Originally established with some aid climbing (A1), it is reportedly possible to lead free. The route ascends sustained granite cracks and corners past named features from the first-ascent account (a 'Confession Box,' 'Pulpit Ledge,' and 'Belfry Ledge') to the summit.
gear: Wide range of nuts and cams to #3 Camalot
fa: Fred Beckey, Dave Wagner, John Brottem, Doug Leen - September 1968
